# What does this PR do?

Add opt-in `--log-dcp-stats` to report estimated attention-work balance and logical-sample CP-size fractions for the **final packed schedule, after VPP alignment**.

The flag defaults to off, with no statistics computed when disabled. It uses the existing log interval and stdout/TensorBoard/W&B writers. Packing and scheduling decisions are unchanged.

## Metrics

For microbatch `m`, `L_i` is sample `i`'s **padded** sequence length, `c[m,i]` is the number of ranks containing its ID, and `R` is the DP×CP rank count, excluding TP/PP replicas:

```text
W[m,r] = sum(L_i² / c[m,i] for each sample i assigned to rank r)
balance = sum_m sum_r W[m,r] / (R × sum_m max_r W[m,r])
```

- `dcp/estimated_attention_balance_efficiency`: closer to 1 means more balanced estimated work. `[8,8,4,4]` gives 0.75. Per-microbatch maxima preserve alternating rank hotspots.
- `dcp/cp_size_<c>_sample_fraction`: each logical ID counts once per microbatch, regardless of CP replication. Equal-length samples with different IDs remain distinct.

Windows accumulate numerators, denominators and counts before division. Empty/zero-work windows omit undefined balance. Packed samples contribute individual squared lengths.

This is a scheduler attention-work estimate, excluding communication, MLP work, pipeline bubbles and some later THD padding. It does not measure GPU utilization.

## Implementation

- A pure CPU helper retains the complete microbatch-by-rank work matrix. The optional `schedule_stats` output preserves the scheduler's four-element return interface.
- TP rank 0 computes statistics after alignment; float64 summaries reuse the existing TP scalar metadata broadcast. No DP/CP collectives are added.
- Pending statistics commit once after a successful update. Reruns reuse the summary; skipped/aborted steps and evaluation do not contribute. TP/PP replicas are not accumulated together.

The [data-loading guide](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/blob/915ffdb5a4d89a3b3f9491ee4d93038cf0985ba2/docs/user-guide/data-loading.md#observing-packed-schedules-and-dynamic-context-parallelism) includes formulas, example logs, limitations and reproduction commands.

## Validation

The runtime code was tested at `79bf7b6bc` on `dev` base `7b66fcc08`, on November 3, 2026 (America/Los_Angeles). The final follow-up updates documentation only. No independent compatibility patch was applied. Current-source benchmark, DP2 logging-window checks, focused regressions and the loop without optimizer updates have now been rerun; the older benchmark is no longer the performance evidence for this source.

### Correctness

**134 focused tests passed per rank on four A6000 GPUs**, with 31 deselected. Coverage includes hand calculations, conservation, CP1/2/4 replication, actual VPP alignment, weighted windows/reset, rerun/skip/exception/eval handling, TP propagation, logger ownership and existing profiling lifecycle checks. The filter omits existing other-topology cases and four unrelated optional-import model-builder cases. The full suite was not run.

All real BF16 training off/on pairs restore identical topology-specific checkpoint, optimizer/scheduler, RNG, seed and data inputs. The following checks compare final schedules, scheduled microbatch counts, losses, gradient hashes and updated parameter hashes:

| Topology | GPUs | Updates per arm | Result |
|---|---:|---:|---|
| DP1/TP1/PP1/CP2 | 2 | 5 | Bitwise off/on equality; CP1/CP2 counts 7/1 |
| DP1/TP2/PP1/CP2 | 4 | 5 | Bitwise off/on equality; TP summary propagation |
| DP1/TP1/PP2/CP2, VPP2 | 4 | 5 | Bitwise off/on equality; alignment changes 3 microbatches to 4 and CP1/CP2 counts to 3/5 |
| DP2/TP1/PP1/CP2 | 4 | 9 | Bitwise off/on equality with varying work, CP fractions and 1–3 microbatches |

The first three topologies have **two DP×CP ranks**; the new DP2×CP2 case has **four**. It uses log interval 3 with interleaved evaluation. An independent verifier reconstructs rank work and window sums from raw schedules:

| Logged iteration | Summed numerator / denominator | CP1 / CP2 logical samples | Balance |
|---|---|---|---:|
| 3 | 2,621,440 / 2,752,512 | 13 / 3 | 0.952381 |
| 6 | 6,881,280 / 6,881,280 | 20 / 4 | 1.000000 |
| 9 | 5,210,112 / 6,520,832 | 18 / 6 | 0.798995 |

All four ranks receive the same global summary, without multiplying counts by rank count. Per-microbatch work conservation, window reset and evaluation exclusion pass. TensorBoard emits exactly once at iterations 3/6/9. The existing first-resumed-iteration stdout report at iteration 2 leaves the window intact; the final partial window at iteration 10 is not emitted. W&B routing has mock-based unit coverage; its external service was not exercised.

The actual `run_train_loop_without_updates` path also passed three iterations on two GPUs with metrics enabled and `--no-load-optim`: the data hook ran each iteration, train_step/statistics never ran, parameters were unchanged, and stdout/TensorBoard had no DCP metrics.

DCP V2 rejects `--deterministic-mode`, so these revalidations omit it while retaining seed 1234, `NVTE_ALLOW_NONDETERMINISTIC_ALGO=0` and `CUBLAS_WORKSPACE_CONFIG=:4096:8`. Observed bitwise equality is not a general determinism guarantee.

### Current-source performance and observation cost

Two A6000 GPUs, TP1/PP1/DP1/CP2, same checkpoint/data/seed and **2,560 effective tokens per update**. Three rotated repetitions per arm, each with 100 updates and the first ten excluded. Timing uses the existing interval timer with stdout/TensorBoard enabled at log interval 1, W&B off, fixed process CPU affinity, no tensor hashing or CPU profiling. Raw GPU telemetry is retained; this is a shared host without locked GPU clocks.

| Arm | Mean step ± between-run std (ms) | Mean effective tokens/s |
|---|---:|---:|
| Fixed CP2 | 142.42 ± 0.40 | 17,975 |
| DCP, metrics off | 117.61 ± 5.39 | 21,796 |
| DCP, metrics on | 116.66 ± 2.25 | 21,949 |

On/off mean step-time difference: **−0.81%**; paired differences **+1.20%, −3.79%, +0.39%**. The variation prevents resolving small overhead. These results do not establish zero overhead or a speedup from enabling metrics. Fixed CP versus DCP compares the existing schedulers on this small workload; this PR does not change their decisions.

Separate CPU diagnostics exclude ten warmups from 40 updates per arm: statistics **40.14–41.43 µs/step**, accumulator update **12.62–13.30 µs/step**. Disabled diagnostic runs make neither call. Emitting-rank logging averages 1.619 ms off / 1.535 ms on, including existing logging/synchronization and host variation. These diagnostic runs are excluded from primary timing aggregates.

[Current-source benchmark and DP2 validation records](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/c9ccb11527135f1ee6351e84447cecd1f64ea855/validation/dcp-stats-acceptance-20261103) retain exact commands, source/checkpoint hashes, environment, raw logs/events/audits, independent verifiers, GPU telemetry and SHA256 manifest. The initial invalid checkpoint-mount timing attempts are retained separately and excluded from all aggregates. Valid timing runs require checkpoint restoration and exactly 100 updates.

[Same-source TP2/PP2/VPP2 rebase records](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/af86402bcd69ca0926bd81af7ffc1978e5f7ee72/validation/dcp-stats-rebase-20261103) retain the other topology comparisons and earlier regression records.

<details>
<summary>Environment, limits and historical records</summary>

RTX A6000/SM86; driver 580.178.04; Python 3.12.4; Torch 2.11.0+cu130; TE 2.20.2; FA2 2.8.3; cuDNN 9.19.0; NCCL 2.28.9. Four-layer dense GPT, hidden 128, FFN 512, four heads, vocabulary 256, sequence limit 1024, zero dropout.

The current dev baseline handles the aligned eager THD padding metadata used here. Internally padded Ampere THD and CUDA Graph execution remain unverified. These real small-model runs use synthetic tokens and do not establish production convergence or scaling.

Repository Black/isort/Pylint/Ruff checks passed. Optional mypy previously reported 12 diagnostics identical to the dev baseline, without new messages. Upstream CI and maintainer review remain separate merge gates. Manual GPU replay scripts are retained with the evidence; a repository functional-test recipe has not been registered.

Historical validation: [October 25–26](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/f0bbe8c22f8740cfae08535ba901d5cafba7a22f/validation/dcp-stats-a6000-20261025) used `87d6973da` on `dd8f93b57` plus an independent eager THD padding adaptation of #7417; [October 29](https://github.com/WEIXILIN0307/Megatron-LM/tree/2bb7c89e25c77f554186fccc449ac022ca1f9043/validation/dcp-stats-rebase-20261029) used the previous `c4220af3a` base. These older records are preserved for provenance.

</details>

## Issue tracking

Related to #6757 and [the proposed scope](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/issues/6757#issuecomment-5945432104). Scope for review: schedule-work estimates interpreted alongside existing training timings.

## Contribution process

- [x] Added relevant unit tests and documentation
- [x] Ran repository formatting checks
- [x] Ran manual GPU training comparisons (records above)
- [ ] Registered functional tests in the repository suite

 This guide covers how Megatron's data pipeline works and how to configure it for efficient training at 256 nodes and beyond. At this scale, the primary bottlenecks are **index building** and **barrier synchronization** -- not raw data bandwidth.
 
+## Observing packed schedules and dynamic context parallelism
+
+Add `--log-dcp-stats` to a training run using `--sequence-packing-scheduler`
+(including `--dynamic-context-parallel`). It defaults to off. The final packed
+schedule is observed **after VPP alignment**, without changing packing or
+scheduling decisions. At the existing `--log-interval`, stdout, TensorBoard and
+W&B emit the metrics below through their existing rank/writer ownership. No new
+monitoring dependency is required. The first-iteration stdout diagnostic retains
+the current window until the regular interval boundary.
+
+For microbatch $m$, let $S_{m,r}$ be the IDs assigned to DP×CP rank $r$,
+$L_i$ the dataset's **padded** sequence length, and
+$c_{m,i}=|\{r:i\in S_{m,r}\}|$ its actual CP size in that microbatch. Then
+
+$$
+W_{m,r}=\sum_{i\in S_{m,r}}\frac{L_i^2}{c_{m,i}},\qquad
+E=\frac{\sum_m\sum_r W_{m,r}}{R\sum_m\max_r W_{m,r}},
+$$
+
+where $R$ is the number of DP×CP ranks, excluding TP and PP replicas. For
+example, $W=[8,8,4,4]$ gives $E=24/(4\times8)=0.75$. Multiple packed samples
+contribute their **individual squares**, not the square of their total length.
+Taking the maximum before summing over microbatches preserves alternating rank
+hotspots. The sum of rank work in each legal microbatch equals the sum of $L_i^2$
+over its unique logical IDs.
+
+- `dcp/estimated_attention_balance_efficiency` reports $E$, closer to 1 for
+  more balanced estimated work. Empty or zero-work windows omit this undefined
+  ratio rather than reporting 100%.
+- `dcp/cp_size_<c>_sample_fraction` reports the fraction of logical samples
+  assigned CP size $c$. Each ID is counted once per microbatch, including when
+  replicated across CP ranks. Equal-length samples with different IDs remain
+  distinct. Only observed CP sizes are emitted.
+
+Logging windows accumulate the efficiency numerator and denominator and CP
+counts before division. TP/PP copies of the global schedule are never added
+together. Reruns reuse one pending summary; only a successful training step
+commits it. Skipped steps, exceptions, early exits and evaluation do not
+contribute. A restart begins a fresh logging window.
+
+Example output (illustrative):
+
+```text
+iteration 100/1000 | dcp/estimated_attention_balance_efficiency: 0.750000 | dcp/cp_size_1_sample_fraction: 0.666667 | dcp/cp_size_2_sample_fraction: 0.333333 | elapsed time per iteration (ms): ...
+```
+
+`L²/CP` is the scheduler's **attention-work estimate**, not measured GPU
+utilization or elapsed-time efficiency. It excludes communication, MLP work,
+pipeline bubbles, and some additional THD padding applied after scheduling.
+Interpret it alongside existing step timing and effective (unmasked) tokens/s.
+Enabling it performs CPU statistics and extends the existing TP scalar metadata
+broadcast using float64 for squared-length precision. There are no additional
+DP/CP collectives; this still has observation and communication overhead.
+The complete microbatch-by-rank work matrix is available from
+`compute_schedule_stats` in `data_schedule_utils.py`, and on TP source ranks via
+the optional `schedule_stats` output dict of `wrap_data_iterator`. The existing
+four-element return value is preserved. No metrics are computed when the dict
+is `None`.
+
+For a small dense BF16/THD DCP run (requires a backend supporting the selected
+GPU and THD padding metadata):
+
+```bash
+python - <<'PY'
+from pathlib import Path
+# Current MockVarlenDataset shifts away one token. These CSV entries yield
+# aligned valid lengths 1024, 256, 128, 512 for the Ampere FA2 path.
+Path('/tmp/dcp-lengths.csv').write_text(('1025\n257\n129\n129\n513\n257\n129\n129\n') * 24)
+PY
+COMMON=(
+  --use-mcore-models --num-layers 4 --hidden-size 128 --ffn-hidden-size 512
+  --num-attention-heads 4 --seq-length 1024 --max-position-embeddings 1024
+  --transformer-impl transformer_engine --attention-backend flash --bf16
+  --attention-dropout 0 --hidden-dropout 0 --no-gradient-accumulation-fusion
+  --micro-batch-size 1 --global-batch-size 8 --calculate-per-token-loss
+  --context-parallel-size 2 --max-seqlen-per-dp-cp-rank 512
+  --use-varlen-dataset --mock-data --tokenizer-type NullTokenizer --vocab-size 256
+  --null-tokenizer-pad-id 0 --num-workers 0 --dataloader-type single
+  --varlen-mock-dataset-config-json '{"mode":"file","format":"thd","path":"/tmp/dcp-lengths.csv"}'
+  --train-iters 40 --lr-decay-iters 100 --lr 0.00015 --min-lr 0.00001
+  --lr-warmup-iters 0 --seed 1234 --log-interval 1 --eval-iters 0
+)
+python -m torch.distributed.run --standalone --nproc-per-node 2 pretrain_gpt.py \
+  "${COMMON[@]}" --dynamic-context-parallel --log-dcp-stats
+```
+

+off/on from the same checkpoint, data and seed, exclude warmup, alternate the
+order and repeat measurements. Verify schedules, microbatch counts, losses,
+gradients and parameter updates before interpreting timing. For fixed CP use
+`--sequence-packing-scheduler dp_balanced` in place of
+`--dynamic-context-parallel`. The existing

+not production-scale convergence or scaling evidence.

+`--pipeline-model-parallel-size 2 --num-layers-per-virtual-pipeline-stage 1
+--microbatch-group-size-per-virtual-pipeline-stage 2`). The latter has **two DP×CP ranks**,
+not four. Confirm that the workload actually triggers VPP alignment; requesting
+VPP alone does not prove that microbatches were split.

+no training step or statistics computation ran, parameters remained unchanged,

+DP2 logging-window results are recorded below.
+[Rebase records and replay commands](https://github.com/Pinoeer-kingxi/Megatron-LM/tree/evidence/dcp-stats-rebase-20261103/validation/dcp-stats-rebase-20261103)
+retain the source/checkpoint hashes, environment, tests, training logs and audits.
+

+        if vpp:

+                pytest.skip('VPP alignment case requires at least four ranks')
+            lengths = [512, 256, 128, 128, 256, 128, 128]
+            unaligned = DefaultDynamicCPScheduler(256, 2, 1, None).get_groups_and_subsamples(

+        samples = []

+                    labels=torch.zeros(length, dtype=torch.int64, device='cuda'),
+                    position_ids=torch.arange(length, device='cuda'),
